text:
Jordan Martinook is 34 and playing exactly the role he has played for most of 575 games in Carolina: a checking winger who makes good teams better. The Hurricanes won the Stanley Cup last season and have won eight of his last ten games this season.

The five-on-five numbers are the reason he keeps getting the job. Carolina controls 61% of the expected goals (chance quality) with him on the ice, and his own chances (0.98 expected goals per 60) are up from 0.79 last season. He has 5 goals and 12 points in 25 games, none on the power play, which is right in our talent range for him.

Evolving-Hockey offers the caution: he plays with strong teammates (93rd percentile by their impact), which flatters raw on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 27% of his entries, so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck, which fits Carolina's style perfectly.

He scored twice against Chicago on Nov. 7 and added an empty-netter against the Rangers. Nothing flashy, nothing fake: a veteran whose numbers match what you see.
headline: Martinook, still the glue in Carolina
